name: Bank of America Student Leaders Program

description: Proof-based math olympiad · advanced

name: Bay Area Science Festival Discovery Fair

description: Local Indian/South Asian cultural orgs in Bay Area run annual student competitions: BAPS Youth Programs, HSS academic contests, Tamil/Telugu/Kannada/Marathi association essay and cultural competitions, Indo American Community Center events.

notes: Check: BAPS (Milpitas/Sunnyvale), HSS Bay Area, Tamil Sangam, Telugu Association NorCal

name: Bryan Cameron Education Foundation Scholarship
description: Merit-based scholarship for HS seniors showing leadership, service, and academic excellence.

notes: NorCal coastal communities especially relevant — Sonoma/Marin/SF/Santa Cruz

description: K-12 students build actual working prototypes to solve real problems. Serves: Alameda, Contra Costa, Marin, Monterey, Napa, San Benito, SF, San Joaquin, San Mateo, Santa Clara, Santa Cruz, Solano, and Sonoma Counties. Free 10-week curriculum. $25 registration. Winners advance to US Nationals.
deadline: Student reg closes Apr 2, 2026; Event Apr 18 (CA State Railroad Museum, Sacramento)
notes: MOST RELEVANT for Sonoma students. Must build actual prototype. $25 fee.

name: California Middle School State Championship

name: Conrad Challenge

notes: $10,000 top prize per category; NASA partnership; highly prestigious.

name: Coolidge Scholarship
description: Full merit scholarship for exceptional young Americans. Full 4-year college funding.
notes: Full 4-year college scholarship

name: CyberPatriot – National Youth Cyber Defense

name: DECA Competitions (Emerging Leaders / ICDC)

notes: ICDC attended by 20,000+ students. Covers 60+ competitive event categories. Strong for business/entrepreneurship track. Scholarships available.

name: Destination Imagination (DI)

name: Destination Imagination (K-2)
notes: Team creativity, low stakes.

name: Diana Award
description: Named after Princess Diana; most prestigious award for young people's social action. Ages 9-25.

name: DiscoverE Future City Engineering Competition
description: Teams of grades 6–8 students imagine, design, and build a model of a future city addressing STEM sustainability themes. $7,500 scholarship for regional first-place winner.
notes: $7,500 scholarship to 1st place regional winner; very accessible for middle schoolers

name: Doodle for Google
description: Students design their own Google Doodle around an annual theme. National winner's art appears on the Google homepage. Open to K-12 students across the U.S.

name: eCYBERMISSION

deadline: State competitions spring; National Conference June
notes: 250,000+ members. Very accessible — most schools have chapters. Strong for business and finance-focused students.

name: FIRST LEGO League (FLL)

notes: Best hub; sign up for email alerts at futureengineers.org

name: Future Problem Solving (FPSPI)
description: Creative problem solving · individual or team

notes: $10,000 prize

name: HOSA – Future Health Professionals ILC

notes: Must join a HOSA chapter through school. Covers 60+ health science events. Very strong for pre-med / health-focused students.

name: India Philanthropy Alliance - youth essay contest
description: Are you passionate about changing the world for the better? This is your chance! Join the IPA Youth Essay Competition and shine a light on an issue that is important to you. This is a great opportunity to find your voice and be a force for good in the world!
deadline: The deadline to participate is July 1, 2026

name: International Eco-Hero Award
description: Action for Nature awards young people who have made measurable impact on local environments. Recognizes outstanding environmental projects by youth worldwide.
notes: 1st Place (age 8–12 group) confirmed. Very competitive international field.

description: Online policy debate and research competition. Teams research a global policy question and submit written arguments; top teams compete live at NYU Finals Weekend. $10,000 prize. 2025-26 topic: G20 global education tax.
notes: $10,000 prize; combines research writing + live debate; held at NYU. Very strong for policy-interested students.

name: International Science and Engineering Fair (ISEF) – Regeneron
description: World's largest international pre-college STEM research competition. Students qualify through affiliated regional fairs (e.g., SVSEF, Sacramento). Top projects across 21 categories compete for $9M+ in prizes. ~1,800 students from 70+ countries.
deadline: Qualify via regional fair spring; ISEF May
notes: Qualify via regional ISEF-affiliated fair. $9M+ in awards. Top U.S. science research competition. Path: SVSEF/Sacramento → ISEF.

name: Invention Convention Worldwide — All State Programs
description: Hub listing ALL state/regional invention conventions: CT, ID, GA Tech, IL, AZ, FL, AL, Kansas City, TN, NC, and more. Use to find programs or enter as independent inventor.
notes: Also: NAI Student Showcase June 1-4 LA (conflicts with RTX Nationals)

description: Prestigious international essay competition in 10 categories: Philosophy, Politics, Economics, History, Psychology, Theology, Law, IR, Public Policy, Science & Tech. Grand Prize $10,000; 1st per category $5,000. 63,000+ entries in 2025 from 150+ countries.
notes: Theology category historically has the smallest applicant pool (~50 shortlisted).

name: Junior Achievement Company Program

notes: Very strong for entrepreneurship-focused students; national competition pathway.

name: Local Debate Classes (Pleasanton/Tri-Valley)
description: Where to take classes & train year-round

description: Berkeley · San Francisco · Stanford

name: NASA Power to Explore (K-4)

notes: Free to enter; multiple grade band prizes

description: Middle/high school teams design and propose science or tech experiments to fly on a NASA high-altitude balloon or suborbital platform. Winners receive $1,500 + NASA starter kit then BUILD the payload for actual flight.

notes: Real payload flies on actual NASA flight — $1,500 + starter kit

notes: High school MUN conferences held nationwide; good gateway to college-level NMUN

name: National Science Bowl (MS)
notes: Team of 4-5.

name: National Science Bowl – Middle School
description: DOE-sponsored academic quiz: biology, chemistry, physics, earth science, math. Nationals in DC.

name: National YoungArts Foundation (All Disciplines)

name: Odyssey of the Mind (Primary)
notes: Fun team division.

name: USACO (USA Computing Olympiad)
